title: Section-normalized tensor evaluation on the ringed sequence site
statement: Let J be an essentially small site with object and morphism universes c,v and coefficients max(c,v,r), and B,\tau an inverse sequence of commutative ring sheaves. Fix a level n. Use the actual Systems, DS and evaluation functors of [def-coef-semilinear-system-models], and choose closed structures and CoefficientTensorModels on the sequence site and on (J,B_n), as in [def-coef-semilinear-derived-calculus]. There is a natural isomorphism e_n(X tensor Y) \cong  e_n X tensor e_n Y together with TensorComparisonModel for these exact chosen models; its ordinary comparison is ordinaryEvaluationTensor on every pair of module sheaves. Thus the chain summands and K-flat representative square are fixed, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism between the same objects.

source.place: Construction 4.1: evaluation on systems; original existence proof step 3.

proof.text: The uniquely pure-section-normalized ordinaryEvaluationTensor is natural in both modules: precompose with its inverse, test on local pure tensors, and use functoriality of the pure tensor section. Evaluation has the existing sectionwise coextension right adjoint, so it preserves the coproducts used in totalization.

Apply the existing signed total construction tensorPullbackTotal to the inverse ordinary comparisons. Its naturality gives a bifunctor isomorphism, and the coproduct inclusion equation gives exactly the required tensorSummand identity.

The coefficient functor rings J B tau gives the same sequence ring as systemSequenceRing. The structural ring maps of the two evaluation interfaces agree componentwise. Transport the already proved systemSequenceEvaluation_preservesKFlat along this functor equality to obtain preservation of the flat-term K-flat representative class.

Resolve homotopy-category objects by flat-term K-flat complexes. The generic resolving-representative whiskering theorem supplies fully faithful restriction on pairs. Apply tensorComparisonDescent to the signed chain isomorphism, the exact evaluation localization factors, and the two given tensor-model comparisons. Cancel the model isomorphisms to obtain the derived field of TensorComparisonModel. Its ordinary field is the original comparison by construction.

lean.statement:
theorem semilinearTensorEvaluation (n : ℕ)
    (closed : Closed.{c, v, r} (coefficientSequenceTopology J)
      (systemRing.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ))
    (models : Models.{c, v, r} (coefficientSequenceTopology J)
      (systemRing.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ) closed)
    (level : Closed.{c, v, r} J (B n)) (levelModels : Models.{c, v, r} J (B n) level) :
    ∃ (γ : closed.tensor ⋙ e.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ n ≅
        ((e.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ n).prod
          (e.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ n)) ⋙ level.tensor)
      (model : TensorComparisonModel.{c, v, r} (coefficientSequenceTopology J) J
        (systemRing.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ) (B n)
        (evaluation.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ n) closed level models levelModels γ),
      ∀ M N : Systems.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ,
        model.ordinary M N = ordinaryEvaluationTensor.{c, v, r} J B τ n M N
